title: m5stack/m5stack-linux-dtoverlays #20 round 4: the 19 s gap is a journald timestamp-base artifact, not a slow restart; confirmed at code level and by arithmetic

firmware.note: unchanged since round 3; no new commit in this round

execution.environment: macOS arm64; no Cardputer Zero hardware; Device Service cardputer-zero supported=false creatable=false backend_ready=false (linux-arm64 backend, __missing_qemu__/__missing_rom__); no kernel headers

checks.name: journald_kmsg_entry_timestamp
checks.evidence: systemd v257 server_dispatch_message_real(): comment plus event_dual_timestamp_now(); entry time is processing time, not source time

checks.name: journald_policy_longstanding
checks.evidence: same policy and comment present in v252 src/journal/journald-server.c:820-836, so not a new-version behaviour

checks.name: kernel_time_only_in_source_fields
checks.evidence: dev_kmsg_record() writes the kmsg usec as _SOURCE_BOOTTIME_TIMESTAMP and _SOURCE_MONOTONIC_TIMESTAMP only

checks.name: timestamp_arithmetic
checks.evidence: prev base 02:13:55.558; kernel start 02:46:03.186-04.185; gap 8.43-9.43 s; driver <= 1.70 s; journal line +9.91-10.90 s

checks.name: no_new_commit_or_code_delta
checks.evidence: head 3b6d273 unchanged; no new commits; mergeable=MERGEABLE; previous 32-scenario/127-check result still applies

checks.name: on_device_hardware
checks.evidence: no Cardputer Zero; author timings (4.1/4.9 s, 15.7 s backstop, fsck-clean boot) not independently reproduced

checks.name: virtual_device
checks.evidence: cardputer-zero uses a separate Linux backend; supported=false, backend_ready=false, missing QEMU and ROM

checks.name: board_systemd_version
checks.evidence: no shell on the board; checked v252 and v257 sources instead of the image's journald binary

checks.name: reset_vs_firmware_split
checks.evidence: the 6.73-7.73 s before the kernel cannot be split between emergency_restart() and firmware boot from the pasted log

evidence.description: systemd v257 and v252 excerpts showing the entry timestamp is the processing time and the kernel time is kept in _SOURCE_* fields
derived previous-boot base, kernel start range, gap decomposition and journal offset
PR state, head, commit list and comment timeline
redacted local Device Service cardputer-zero profile and why it is not runnable

notes: Evidence class is code-level verification plus arithmetic on the author's log anchors; no runtime reproduction.
The 19.333 s interval decomposes into ~8.4-9.4 s of real reset/boot plus ~10-11 s of journald start delay, so it does not contradict the 1.5 s + <=200 ms restart path.
No code change is requested in this round; the only open item from the previous review is closed.
An inherent <=200 ms window remains between the last .shutdown sample and the halt; both sides agree it cannot be closed.
